newsitem.title: CHINA: Gore to attend China pacts with Boeing, GM.
newsitem.headline: Gore to attend China pacts with Boeing, GM.

text.p: Boeing Co will sign a contract in Beijing on Tuesday to sell China five 777-200 jets worth $685 million at a ceremony attended by U.S. Vice President Al Gore, White House officials said.

Gore also planned to witness a formal agreement in which General Motors Corp will enter into a joint venture with state-owned Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp to build car engines and transmissions in China, the officials said.
"These agreements ... are proof positive that there is greater economic cooperation between the United States and China," said Ginny Terzano, Gore's press secretary.
She denied reports that Gore, on a trip to China aimed at improving relations, had been uncertain whether he should witness the Boeing contract signing -- which has been rumoured for several days.
"There was never any reluctance," she said. She was

countering reports that Gore hesitated to attend the ceremony because of allegations that China had tried to influence last year's U.S. presidential election by illegally funnelling cash to support President Bill Clinton's campaign.
The cost of the $1.3 billion motor project, to be built in Shanghai, will be shared equally by the two corporations.
The project received an initial go-ahead in 1995 but final approval has been subject to lengthy delays.
In the aviation agreement, the Civil Aviation Administration of China will order five 777-200s for Air China, with three of the jets to be delivered by the end of 1998 and the other two in 1999.
Under a third agreement to be signed on Tuesday, China will formally allow the United States to continue to operate a consulate in Hong Kong once 150 years of British control ends on June 30.
The accords are to be signed at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing starting at 0300 GMT.
